top.title: Ian Rush calls out bizarre Alexander Isak criticism after electric start rivals Haaland
top.description: Ian Rush calls out bizarre Alexander Isak criticism after electric start rivals Haaland Ian Rush has disagreed with the common consensus about Alexander Isak this season. The Swedish international has been accused, at various times this season, of not being actively involved during Liverpool games. But Alexander Isak is scoring – and that’s what matters! (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) As Rush was at pains to point out, the former Newcastle United hitman is scoring goals this season. Enough, at any rate, to put him in early contention with Manchester City’s Erling Haaland for the golden boot, with seven Premier League goals registered to the Norwegian’s nine – and in one fewer game to boot. “People say that Isak isn’t getting involved much but he’s scoring goals and that’s all that matters. The hardest thing in football is to score a goal and he’s only second to (Erling) Haaland,” the Liverpool legend told BBC Sport . It seems that no matter what the 27-year-old does in the famous red shirt, someone will have something negative to say about his performances. But the fact remains that Isak is managing to get on the scoresheet with some degree of frequency as part of a frontline that is far from cohesive at this stage. Can you imagine how many times he’ll be finding the back of the net once he finds a collective rhythm alongside Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola? Critics forget what Isak went through at Liverpool last term (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) One may reasonably be inclined to think that critics have forgotten how Isak had the debut season from hell at Liverpool following his move from Newcastle in the summer. The forward managed only 1,032 minutes across all competitions in Arne Slot’s final season in charge, between adductor issues and a broken fibula. 1,032 minutes, four goals and one assist. In 2026/27, the Swede has already racked up eight goals and an assist in 899 minutes of action (across all competitions). Far easier for Alexander Isak to build fluency when he’s spending a lot more time on the pitch early in the season and stringing a series of starts together from one game to the next.

top.title: Official: Brock Faber Returns to MN Wild Blue Line
top.description: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild are in Boston on Saturday trying to add more points to their already gawdy total of 32, the most in both the Central Division and Western Conference. Entering tonight’s matchup, the Wild have a 98% chance of making the playoffs , according to multiple models and sportsbooks. Even more impressive, they’ve done it all without top-line defenseman, Brock Faber. The former Gopher fractured his skull on Sept. 25 when a puck hit him in the side of the head during the Wild’s preseason finale against Dallas. He had surgery two days later, spent three days at Regions Hospital and has missed all 21 regular season games since. Doctors cleared Faber to practice in early November. By Nov. 12, head coach John Hynes confirmed that the target date for his return was Saturday, but there were “no guarantees.” As recent as Friday, there were real doubts over whether or not Faber would hit that date, or wait Tuesday when the Wild return home against Nashville. Minnesota Wild activate Brock Faber for his season debut But then Saturday morning, the Wild made it official, activating Faber from injured reserve, and announcing on social media that the 24-year-old defenseman is back. Hynes confirmed the debut, according to Joe O’Donnell (Wild radio). Michael Russo (The Athletic) reported that Joel Eriksson Ek will play as well. The #mnwild has activated defenseman Brock Faber from Injured Reserve. — Minnesota Wild PR (@mnwildPR) November 14, 2026 we can think of exactly 7 reasons to be happy today — Minnesota Wild (@minnesotawild) November 14, 2026 Related: MN Wild Getting Healthier Again; Faber Back…? The defense pairs aren’t set yet. Russo listed two options , with Faber skating next to either Quinn Hughes or Jonas Brodin, and Olli Maatta and Zach Bogosian together on the third pair. A win against the Bruins would add to a 10-game point streak and mark seven straight road victories all without Brock Faber. What are MN Wild getting back with Faber’s return? Last season, the Maple Grove native had career highs of 15 goals and 51 points in 80 games, with 36 assists and a plus-18. His 15 goals led Wild defensemen and tied for 10th among all NHL defensemen. Faber averaged 24:41 of ice time, second on the team behind Hughes. He’s now in year two of an eight-year, $68 million contract that carries an $8.5 million cap hit through 2032-33. Faber and the Wild face the Bruins (13-5-1) tonight at 6 p.m. CT at TD Garden on Wild+ and Fubo. Russo reported that Jesper Wallstedt will start in goal against Jeremy Swayman. top.title: Minnesota Vikings’ Kirk Cousins Trade Features Interesting Twist
top.description: The Minnesota Vikings made a move to acquire quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders at the NFL trade deadline, sending a third-round pick to the Raiders in return. The deal followed the Vikings’ miserable Week 9 Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills, where Minnesota managed just six points in a 17-point defeat. Carson Wentz managed just 81 passing yards before being benched for Max Brosmer. That appeared to be the tipping point for the Vikings, who started the 2026 campaign 6-0 but have now lost two games in a row to watch their NFC North lead disappear. However, Minnesota had apparently reached a boiling before before the Bills loss, according to NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. Minnesota Vikings tried to trade for Kirk Cousins earlier Oct 23, 2023; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) warms up before the game against the San Francisco 49ers at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-USA TODAY Sports Evidently, the Vikings reached out to the Raiders before Monday night’s disaster. “The first time the Vikings reached out to the Raiders about a potential trade for Kirk Cousins was midday Monday, hours before Minnesota played the Bills on ‘Monday Night Football,’ league sources told ESPN and NFL Network,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote . “During that call, the Vikings made it clear to the Raiders that they wanted to see how Monday night went first before having any further conversations about Cousins, but they would be in touch if needed.” Obviously, things ended up going very south for the Vikings in that game, so that was when they ultimately decided to pull the trigger. Of course, Minnesota may have incidentally given Las Vegas more leverage in those trade discussions considering just how bad the Vikings looked under center on Monday, but a third-round pick seemed like a small price to pay for Minnesota. Cousins is now in his second stint with the Vikings after spending six years with the club between 2018 and 2023. The 38-year-old is certainly armed with an impressive stable of weapons in Minnesota, so we’ll see if he can ultimately lead the Vikings on a deep playoff run. top.description: Ravichandran Ashwin has opened up about an emotional conversation with Virat Kohli at the Gabba during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy, recalling how the former India captain was left emotional after learning about his decision to retire from international cricket. The former India off-spinner revealed that the conversation took place on the balcony in Brisbane during a rain interruption. What began as an informal discussion between the two eventually turned into a heartfelt exchange, with Kohli speaking about the future of India's Test team and the challenges surrounding its transition. Speaking on a podcast with Aakash Chopra, Ashwin explained that retirement had been on his mind for several months before he finally called time on his career in December 2024. He disclosed that he had first contemplated the decision as early as March 2024, despite enjoying an excellent run with the ball. However, persistent knee problems were affecting his batting. Head coach Gautam Gambhir subsequently urged him to continue until the end of India's 2024 home season. The home Test series against New Zealand, in which India suffered a whitewash, proved particularly disappointing for Ashwin. He felt he was no longer able to deliver match-winning performances for the team. His decision became firmer after he was left out of India's playing XI for the opening Test against Australia in Perth. When an opportunity arose during the Brisbane Test, Ashwin found himself alone with Kohli during a rain break and decided to share his thoughts. “In that game, I didn’t go there to tell Virat and it was raining; I sat with him only because he was sitting alone," Ashwin remembered. Ashwin also reflected on how his relationship with Kohli had evolved over the years. The two had experienced differences in the past, but the former spinner said their equation improved following the COVID break. During their conversation at the Gabba, Kohli began discussing his own batting, the state of the Indian Test side and the challenges ahead during a period of transition. “My relationship with Virat improved after the COVID break. I realized that if there were any disappointments in my mind, it wasn’t his fault. I tried to speak to him about that; I was forthcoming. I had nothing selfish to to say. But he started speaking his mind: what he was thinking about his batting, how he looked at the Indian Test team, what it needed in a transition. He was talking like a leader, how there were these basic problems in the team and so on. I listened." The conversation took an unexpected turn when Kohli sought Ashwin's opinion on the team's future. top.title: Give J.J. McCarthy a quicker late-game answer for the Giants
top.description: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) looks to throw the ball during a game against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium, Nov 12, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect On Friday, John Harbaugh said the Giants had short and deep routes available on the late throws against Washington’s all-out pressure. I’d change the order of the decision for J.J. McCarthy. With a field goal still useful and the clock running out, decide before the snap which underneath throw can keep the drive alive. Take the deep ball when the look is right, not because pressure narrowed the quarterback’s time to think. The pressure itself didn’t defeat McCarthy all night. He went 8-for-14 for 155 yards against the blitz, according to Next Gen Stats via John Schmeelk’s Friday review . He also finished with a career-high 293 passing yards. In the final sequence a deep throw intended for Malik Nabers was intercepted with 25 seconds left, per the game recap . You can see a quarterback handle extra rushers well for most of a game and still want a better answer for that last situation. Separate the pressure answer from the clock answer “The ball’s got to come out fast,” Harbaugh said . He noted the offense couldn’t block everyone on the zero blitzes and said McCarthy made split-second choices. A receiver can be open further down the field without being the best throw for the situation. To me, the adjustment is to give McCarthy a short route he can choose at the line and a clear idea of which side he needs the catch to finish on. Nov 12, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) shouts out a call during the second half against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On a down when New York still has time to run another play, I’d bring a receiver across the formation and attach a break toward the boundary at the sticks. Use the movement to see a defender travel and make the throw early enough that the receiver can catch it facing the sideline. If the defense takes away the short route and leaves Nabers on top of his man with room to land the ball, the vertical throw stays in the call. The quarterback isn’t being asked to pass up a touchdown. He’s being asked to know what a useful completion looks like before the rush arrives. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. I’d use that if New York needs a bigger gain, or if there isn’t a credible short route that will stop the clock. The price is one fewer receiver in the pattern, and even adding a blocker might not account for every rusher. Once the game comes down to a final pass, the trade-off changes again. top.title: Alec Bohm makes sense for the Yankees at one guaranteed year
top.description: Oct 1, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies infielder Alec Bohm (28) looks on before game three of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alec Bohm is worth a call if the Yankees want a right-handed answer at third base. I wouldn’t sign him as the answer for all 162 games. My offer would be one guaranteed year, with Ryan McMahon still around to take most of the starts against right-handers and defend late when New York has a lead. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand reported the Yankees’ interest , after Jon Heyman first reported it for the New York Post. Bryan Hoch’s Friday look at the roster says New York is open to adding at third. Neither report establishes a one-year offer. That’s the term I’d be willing to guarantee. Sep 30, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Alec Bohm (28) celebrates in the dugout after hitting a solo home run against the Atlanta Braves in the tenth inning during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees would be buying the matchup, not the entire stat line Bohm finished last season with a .698 OPS. Look at his 2026 splits and you can see two different jobs inside that number: .816 against left-handers in 192 plate appearances and .644 against right-handers in 437. McMahon had a .509 OPS against lefties and .662 against righties. The gap that gives Bohm a job is on the left-handed side of the opposing rotation. There isn’t much evidence in these numbers to make him the default against righties. The fielding is a separate reason not to hand him the full job. Feinsand’s report cites a minus-nine Fielding Run Value in 2026. That’s one measure and a down year, not an exact bill for what will happen in the Bronx. But if New York adds Bohm for the bat, it should be comfortable replacing him for defense when that advantage has already been used and the game is on the line. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. A flexible third-base plan still has a price There will be days the likely second pitcher matters as much as the starter. If the opponent starts a lefty but can go to a right-hander in the fourth, I would keep the option to hit for Bohm later. If McMahon is on the bench and the tying run is on second, you’ve still got a left-handed bat and the ability to finish the game with him at third. Before making the offer, I’d also map out the rest of the bench. Two third basemen are easier to carry if somebody else can cover second and short without starting a chain of substitutions. Bohm’s experience at first helps, but with Ben Rice already there, those innings don’t carry the same value to the Yankees as they might to another club. You can make a case for paying more if you think Bohm’s .794 OPS after the All-Star break is the hitter you’ll get for a whole season.

top.title: Rams Could Acquire 8-Year Veteran WR in Post-Deadline Move
top.description: The Los Angeles Rams are certainly facing an injury crisis at the wide receiver position. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all on injured reserve, and while the Rams are 5-4 and still very much alive in the NFC playoff picture, their offense is on life support. Los Angeles did not add any wide receiver help at the NFL trade deadline, much to the chagrin of the fanbase. And in terms of free agency, the options are very thin at this time of year. However, Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton has identified a potential fit for Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ aerial attack: eight-year veteran receiver Darius Slayton. Los Angeles Rams could sign Darius Slayton New York Giants wide receiver Darius Slayton (18) runs with the ball, Sunday, January 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Slayton was released by the New York Giants before the season. He then signed with the Indianapolis Colts, but was cut before even getting into a game. That leaves the door open for the Rams to sign him. “At 29, Slayton can be a productive perimeter playmaker if he can still stretch defenses in the vertical passing game,” Moton wrote . “… The Los Angeles Rams will be without their top two receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, for the foreseeable future. Matthew Stafford needs an experienced starting wideout to target within the Rams’ depleted pass-catching unit.” Slayton spent the first seven years of his career with the Giants and was a reliable weapon for them, posting over 500 receiving yards in six of his seven campaigns. He also finished with over 700 yards four times. Last year, the former fifth-round pick caught 37 passes for 538 yards and a touchdown, although he struggled with drops. He also underwent core muscle surgery after the season. Slayton wouldn’t be anyone’s favorite option, but he could certainly be of help to a Rams team in dire need of help at the position. top.title: Atiku tackles FG as bakers lose 40% membership
top.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies for the loss of nearly 40 per cent of the membership of the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria in two years, warning that soaring energy costs and high interest rates are driving local businesses out of operation. The development, he said, underscores the growing strain on businesses, with bakeries shutting down, workers losing their jobs and households paying more for bread, one of Nigeria’s everyday staples. Atiku, who was in Bauchi on Saturday to promote his affordable life campaign and sympathise with Nigerians grappling with the effects of government policies, spoke in a statement signed by his Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, and Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu. “From farmers to manufacturers and now bakers, the verdict on Tinubu’s economic reforms cannot be clearer: they have been a monumental failure,” he said. The former vice president identified rising energy costs and expensive credit as major constraints on bakery operations, noting that energy alone accounts for about half of production costs. He cited the case of a bakery operator whose monthly diesel bill reportedly increased from N9 million to N19 million, while small-scale bakeries require between N40 million and N50 million to switch to alternative energy sources. He added that businesses seeking loans face interest rates of up to 34 per cent, further limiting their ability to sustain production and invest in more efficient operations. Atiku said the pressure extends beyond the baking industry, citing rising cooking gas prices, which he said had reached N1,800 per kilogramme in Abuja and N1,650 in parts of Lagos and Ogun states. He also cited a 31.8 per cent increase in depot prices within one month, from N1,100 to N1,450 per kilogramme. Turning to the Federal Government’s borrowing, Atiku questioned the accumulation of domestic and foreign loans amid the reported closure of local businesses, alleging that Nigerians were yet to see tangible benefits from the debt. “The irony is that while the economy is falling under Bola Tinubu’s watch, his government has accumulated local and foreign loans in astronomical figures. If local businesses are dying while the government continues to borrow, Nigerians are entitled to ask where these loans are going. top.title: Columbus Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness remains out with health issue
top.description: Rick Bowness will miss a second straight game due to an undisclosed health issue when the Blue Jackets play the Philadelphia Flyers on Nov. 14 at Nationwide Arena, and his return to the bench is uncertain as he undergoes medical evaluation. More: The Columbus Blue Jackets are still sputtering: Where's the beef? Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell said Bowness, 71, is considered "day-to-day" until more is known about the situation. Bowness hasn't been ruled out for an upcoming four-game road trip that starts Nov. 17 against the New York Islanders, but he won't travel with the team Oct. 16 when it heads to New York. "He's doing more testing on Monday," Waddell said. "He was actually here [at the arena] this morning for a little bit. That's a good sign. He met with the coaches and [all] that. We'll list him like a player, 'day-to-day,' but I've talked to him a lot. He's doing OK. He's just got some things that are affecting him that we need to figure out ... the doctors need to figure out." Bowness missed the Blue Jackets' 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning on Oct. 12 at Nationwide Arena. Assistant coach Don Granato, former head coach of the Buffalo Sabres, handled the head coaching duties. Granato will again run the bench against the Flyers, while assistants Trent Vogelhuber, Jared Boll and goaltending coach Niklas Backstrom will handle their usual tasks. Waddell said the issue became noticeable recently, which led to Bowness getting checked out. "The last couple days, he wasn't feeling great," Waddell said. "He came in Thursday morning, and we told him to go home and get rest because he wasn't 'looking great, and from there we got our doctors involved and we're trying to figure out what's going on." Bowness left retirement to join the Blue Jackets in January 2026, taking over midseason for Dean Evason. His prior coaching job was with the Winnipeg Jets and he cited undisclosed family and health issues as the reason he stepped down from that head coaching role in April 2024. He twice stepped away from the Jets in 2023-24 for family and medical reasons. The first was after his wife, Judy, had a seizure and the second was for a minor medical procedure of his own. Upon joining the Blue Jackets, Bowness said he was physically up to returning as an NHL head coach and that his wife was just as eager for him to do it. nigeria.title: Spain will host 2030 World Cup final, federation president insists
nigeria.description: The 2030 World Cup final will be in Spain, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan reiterated on Saturday, adding that he is not considering “withdrawing” should he be wrong. Spain is organising the next World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. The decision on the venue for the final will be made in 2028, Louzan said. Spain favours Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium for the final. Portugal does not have a suitable stadium but Morocco has suggested the 115,000-capacity Hassan II Stadium being built in Benslimane near Casablanca. “There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” said Louzan at a conference at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Futbol on the outskirts of Madrid. “I am not currently considering the possibility of withdrawing from Spain, as the prospect of Spain not hosting the final is not on the table,” he said. Louzan was responding to Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the right-wing People’s Party. In a television interview on November 5, Feijoo said that were he to become prime minister in the general election on November 29, he would advocate withdrawing Spain’s bid to host the World Cup should Morocco be awarded the final. Luzon said the question was entirely hypothetical. “That notion simply doesn’t exist,” he said, adding that under FIFA’s tradition of rotating the World Cup the staging of the final “belongs to the European continent”. A delegation of FIFA technical experts spent last week visiting Spanish stadiums that are hoping to host matches during the tournament, Louzan said. nigeria.title: FG raises alarm over 2,000 universities, 100 fake professors report
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, ABUJA The Federal Government has dismissed viral claims that Nigeria has 2,000 universities and that about 100 professors in the country were exposed as fake, describing the reports as fabricated misinformation aimed at eroding public confidence in the nation’s university system. The government, through the Federal Ministry of Education, said the National Universities Commission, NUC, never made such declarations, published the alleged list of fake professors or authenticated the names currently circulating on social media. Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, made the clarification in a statement issued on Saturday through the ministry’s Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade. He said the claims were false, misleading and a recycled version of old information being distorted to deceive the public. The ministry specifically faulted reports suggesting that the NUC had identified about 100 individuals as fake professors, explaining that the allegation was a misrepresentation of a media report published on December 3, 2019. According to the ministry, the original report concerned an exercise by the NUC to verify the directory of full professors in Nigerian universities and did not contain the names now being circulated online. It stressed that the commission had since disowned the purported list, insisting that it neither originated from the regulatory agency nor enjoyed its endorsement. 2,000 varsities On the claim that Nigeria has 2,000 universities, the ministry said the NUC had never announced the existence of such a number of universities in the country. The government expressed concern over what it described as the persistent recycling of false information, warning that such claims could undermine the credibility of Nigerian universities and damage efforts to strengthen standards in the nation’s higher education system. It urged media organisations, social media users and members of the public to exercise caution before sharing unverified information, particularly on issues concerning the recognition of universities and the integrity of academic qualifications. The ministry advised Nigerians to rely on the NUC’s official communication channels for accurate information on recognised universities, academic standards and regulatory decisions. It reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to supporting the NUC in protecting academic integrity, strengthening quality assurance and preserving the credibility and international reputation of Nigeria’s university education system. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. Enough, at any rate, to put him in early contention with Manchester City’s Erling Haaland for the golden boot, with seven Premier League goals registered to the Norwegian’s nine – and in one fewer game to boot. “People say that Isak isn’t getting involved much but he’s scoring goals and that’s all that matters. It seems that no matter what the 27-year-old does in the famous red shirt, someone will have something negative to say about his performances. But the fact remains that Isak is managing to get on the scoresheet with some degree of frequency as part of a frontline that is far from cohesive at this stage. Can you imagine how many times he’ll be finding the back of the net once he finds a collective rhythm alongside Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola? Critics forget what Isak went through at Liverpool last term (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) One may reasonably be inclined to think that critics have forgotten how Isak had the debut season from hell at Liverpool following his move from Newcastle in the summer. The forward managed only 1,032 minutes across all competitions in Arne Slot’s final season in charge, between adductor issues and a broken fibula. 1,032 minutes, four goals and one assist. In 2026/27, the Swede has already racked up eight goals and an assist in 899 minutes of action (across all competitions). Far easier for Alexander Isak to build fluency when he’s spending a lot more time on the pitch early in the season and stringing a series of starts together from one game to the next.

Take the deep ball when the look is right, not because pressure narrowed the quarterback’s time to think. The pressure itself didn’t defeat McCarthy all night. sports.title: Alec Bohm makes sense for the Yankees at one guaranteed year
sports.description: Oct 1, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies infielder Alec Bohm (28) looks on before game three of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alec Bohm is worth a call if the Yankees want a right-handed answer at third base. I wouldn’t sign him as the answer for all 162 games. My offer would be one guaranteed year, with Ryan McMahon still around to take most of the starts against right-handers and defend late when New York has a lead. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand reported the Yankees’ interest , after Jon Heyman first reported it for the New York Post. Bryan Hoch’s Friday look at the roster says New York is open to adding at third. Neither report establishes a one-year offer. That’s the term I’d be willing to guarantee. Sep 30, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Philadelphia Phillies first baseman Alec Bohm (28) celebrates in the dugout after hitting a solo home run against the Atlanta Braves in the tenth inning during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Yankees would be buying the matchup, not the entire stat line Bohm finished last season with a .698 OPS. Look at his 2026 splits and you can see two different jobs inside that number: .816 against left-handers in 192 plate appearances and .644 against right-handers in 437. McMahon had a .509 OPS against lefties and .662 against righties. The gap that gives Bohm a job is on the left-handed side of the opposing rotation. There isn’t much evidence in these numbers to make him the default against righties. The fielding is a separate reason not to hand him the full job. Feinsand’s report cites a minus-nine Fielding Run Value in 2026. That’s one measure and a down year, not an exact bill for what will happen in the Bronx. But if New York adds Bohm for the bat, it should be comfortable replacing him for defense when that advantage has already been used and the game is on the line. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. A flexible third-base plan still has a price There will be days the likely second pitcher matters as much as the starter. If the opponent starts a lefty but can go to a right-hander in the fourth, I would keep the option to hit for Bohm later. If McMahon is on the bench and the tying run is on second, you’ve still got a left-handed bat and the ability to finish the game with him at third. Before making the offer, I’d also map out the rest of the bench. Two third basemen are easier to carry if somebody else can cover second and short without starting a chain of substitutions. Bohm’s experience at first helps, but with Ben Rice already there, those innings don’t carry the same value to the Yankees as they might to another club. You can make a case for paying more if you think Bohm’s .794 OPS after the All-Star break is the hitter you’ll get for a whole season.

sports.description: Rick Bowness will miss a second straight game due to an undisclosed health issue when the Blue Jackets play the Philadelphia Flyers on Nov. 14 at Nationwide Arena, and his return to the bench is uncertain as he undergoes medical evaluation. More: The Columbus Blue Jackets are still sputtering: Where's the beef? Blue Jackets president/general manager Don Waddell said Bowness, 71, is considered "day-to-day" until more is known about the situation. Bowness hasn't been ruled out for an upcoming four-game road trip that starts Nov. 17 against the New York Islanders, but he won't travel with the team Oct. 16 when it heads to New York. "He's doing more testing on Monday," Waddell said. "He was actually here [at the arena] this morning for a little bit. That's a good sign. He met with the coaches and [all] that. We'll list him like a player, 'day-to-day,' but I've talked to him a lot. He's doing OK. He's just got some things that are affecting him that we need to figure out ... the doctors need to figure out." Bowness missed the Blue Jackets' 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning on Oct. 12 at Nationwide Arena. Assistant coach Don Granato, former head coach of the Buffalo Sabres, handled the head coaching duties. Granato will again run the bench against the Flyers, while assistants Trent Vogelhuber, Jared Boll and goaltending coach Niklas Backstrom will handle their usual tasks. Waddell said the issue became noticeable recently, which led to Bowness getting checked out. "The last couple days, he wasn't feeling great," Waddell said. "He came in Thursday morning, and we told him to go home and get rest because he wasn't 'looking great, and from there we got our doctors involved and we're trying to figure out what's going on." Bowness left retirement to join the Blue Jackets in January 2026, taking over midseason for Dean Evason. His prior coaching job was with the Winnipeg Jets and he cited undisclosed family and health issues as the reason he stepped down from that head coaching role in April 2024. He twice stepped away from the Jets in 2023-24 for family and medical reasons. The first was after his wife, Judy, had a seizure and the second was for a minor medical procedure of his own. Upon joining the Blue Jackets, Bowness said he was physically up to returning as an NHL head coach and that his wife was just as eager for him to do it. Five years of dominance, taking care of business against its smaller crosstown rival. A “little brother” of sorts. That was not the case on Friday night. In fact, the roles were reversed. Northwestern was the “little brother.” Literally. Both smaller in size and in depth, the Blue Demons exposed the Wildcats’ Achilles’ heel in their 20-point win. “Our offense really struggled tonight,” said head coach Chris Collins in his postgame presser. “A lot of it had to do with [DePaul]: their switching, their physicality, their ball pressure. I thought when the game was in the balance, we had a number of opportunities where we left points on the table in the open floor.” Separation was nowhere to be found for NU in this one; its largest lead was two points, and it’s because of personnel. DePaul’s pair of 7-footers Fabian Flores and Magoon Gwath anchored the Blue Demon defense, combining for 14 rebounds and four blocks on the night. DePaul finished with 45 and 11 in those categories, respectively, as its guards supplemented its play down low with relentless aggression and physicality, turning the game into a complete scrap. And Depaul won in the margins where Northwestern lacked. Collins didn’t avoid that. He took responsibility for it. “[Ade] Popoola had three offensive rebounds, [Noah] Meeusen had four — he’s the point guard. [He] wasn’t 7-foot. That’s seven offensive rebounds from their two guards. You got to come out, and you got to compete.” In a world where 20% of last year’s roster returned for the 2026-27 season, this rendition of the Wildcats eerily reflects what ‘Cats faithful saw last year: a small unit that struggled to keep opponents off the glass, giving up far too many second-chance points that its offense couldn’t make up. Collins says it’s not fair to compare this year’s squad to last year’s in that same press conference, but if you’re a Northwestern fan, it’s awfully hard not to right now. technology.description: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are. Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths. science.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
science.description: null LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing. For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. It's just — it's overwhelming," former NASA astronaut Garrett Reisman told Space.com during a visit to the museum. Reisman flew on two space shuttle missions during his astronaut career, the first of which was on Endeavour. The space shuttle Endeavour. science.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
science.description: null Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars. In fact, you're likely to catch their collective brightness in your peripheral vision every time you go outside and look up. But every November the Pleiades remind me that naked-eye observing isn't as simple as opening the back door and looking up. How many Pleiades I can see can change depending on what I do during the next 10 minutes. What's happening and when to look You can easily see the Pleiades as a bright misty patch in your peripheral vision during winter. (Image credit: Haitong Yu via Getty Images) The Pleiades, also known as Messier 45 (M45) or the "Seven Sisters," are an open star cluster in Taurus. They're one of the closest clusters to the solar system and some of the youngest stars you can see with the naked eye — just 100 million years old. They're basically newborns. In mid-November, they rise in the east in the early evening and climb higher as the night progresses, making this an excellent time to get acquainted with them. Look east after dark for a tiny, compact group of stars. If you know Orion, which rises later, the Pleiades are above and to the right of it from mid-northern latitudes. Nearby you'll also find orange Aldebaran and the much broader V-shaped Hyades cluster. The Hyades are closer to the sun , but their stars are about 625 million years old. The name "Seven Sisters" creates an immediate observational trap: people assume they're supposed to see seven stars. That's not necessarily true. In fact, six is a common naked-eye result under decently dark conditions (note that the shape of the six brightest is like a mini Big Dipper /Plough), while people with sharp eyesight under darker skies may see more. The cluster itself contains about 1,000 stars. The number you personally distinguish depends on eyesight, sky brightness, atmospheric conditions and how well your eyes have adapted to darkness. science.title: 'Martian Isolation' is an upcoming sci-fi survival horror game that looks like 'The Martian' and 'Event Horizon' had a horrific child
science.description: null "Martian Isolation" is an upcoming single-player, first-person survival horror game that's just been revealed with a suitably creepy launch trailer. And yes, it does look an awful lot like " The Martian ," doesn't it? There's a lot of survival gameplay on display here that mirrors Mark Watney's tale of survival on the Red Planet, as your stranded protagonist is forced to explore the Martian surface to acquire resources, grow plants, and repair their base. That comparison to Andy Weir's sci-fi masterpiece does fall away as you get further into the trailer, though, when the horror part of the game's description comes into play: Flickering lights, creepy figures stalking the halls of your Martian habitat, and blood dripping from the walls. Oh yeah, that's some good creepy sci-fi horror right there. It's giving " Event Horizon ", and that's always getting a thumbs-up from me. There's no release date scheduled at this time, with the 'Martian Isolation' Steam page simply listing it as "coming soon," though the YouTube trailer description does say it "will be available on Steam in 2027". You can't pre-order yet, but if this looks like your jam, you can add it to your wishlist. Beyond that, we know shockingly little about this title. It's the debut game from Golden Milestone Studio, but there's very little information out there beyond a name. The latest blog post on the game's Steam page says that they're a "small team," but what we've seen so far is encouraging. There seems to be a pronounced split between the survival and horror elements of the game along the day/night cycle. Daytime sees you exploring the Martian surface, smashing rocks, cleaning solar panels, and doing sick jumps on a quad bike. The psychological torment only begins once the sun goes down (they mostly come out at night … mostly), as your character starts encountering cosmic horrors and weird naked zombie men. Mars rover, nice. Golden Milestone Studio Spacesuits, check. Golden Milestone Studio Crafting, of course. Golden Milestone Studio OH SWEET JESUS! Get it away, get it away. Golden Milestone Studio OK, we're good. Mining, cool. Golden Milestone Studio Riding a quad bike on Mars, yes please. Golden Milestone Studio Growing potatoes on Mars, just like that guy in the movie. Golden Milestone Studio Opening a box with power tools, seems excessive but sure. Golden Milestone Studio NOPE! Nope, nope, nope, I'm out! Golden Milestone Studio Are they hallucinations, or is there some malevolent presence hiding in the blood-red sands of Mars ? I'm always looking for new ways to shatter my psyche and possibly soil my pants, so I'll be keeping a close eye on this one. In the meantime, I do need to get back and finish " Routine ." I left my character hiding under a desk months ago, and I haven't been brave enough to go back. As Mama always said, you can't have any Martian horror until you finish your lunar horror first.

science.title: Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star
science.description: null Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star. The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153. GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021. Several previously discovered LPT systems contain a white dwarf and a companion star, but it has been unclear which of the two stars was generating the radio pulses. That means the discovery of GPM J071507−114153 and finding that the pulses come from close to the white dwarf could be a significant step toward understanding the nature of LPTs. The unusual system consists of a small and highly energetic white dwarf pulsar, orbiting a much larger star similar to our sun. (Image credit: ICRAR) "This is the first time the pulses are clear enough to see the white dwarf moving in its orbit around its companion," team leader and commissioning scientist with the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKA), Sam McSweeney, said in a statement . "So we know that the pulsations are coming from a region close to the white dwarf, or possibly even from the white dwarf itself." The pulses seen by the team also allowed them to detect stellar flares erupting on the sun-like star. "As a bonus, we also saw the white dwarf moving behind a region with a strong magnetic field, most likely a 'stellar prominence,' which is a large loop of plasma erupting from a star's surface," team member Natasha Hurley-Walker of the International Centre for Radio Astronomy Research (ICRAR), Curtin University, Australia, said. "It's amazing that by using radio wavelengths we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away." South Africa’s MeerKAT telescope. (Image credit: South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO)) Hurley-Walker and the team at ICRAR have been at the cutting edge of rare star systems like this. "We detected this system in a large survey using the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) to scan the entire Milky Way visible from Australia," Hurley-Walker said. "We then used the MeerKAT radio telescope in South Africa to determine its precise position." After the radio telescopes detected this LPT, it was confirmed using the W.M. Keck Observatory on Maunakea in Hawaii. The visible light follow-up of Keck also confirmed that the star in GPM J071507−114153 was a G-type star, just like the sun. science.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
science.description: NASA astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured this image of the area surrounding the Red Sea and Nile river valley on November 14, 1966, during their four-day mission in space. Gemini XII was the final flight of NASA’s Gemini Program. NASA Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII , the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of a different field of exploration, observing Earth from space. The photos taken by Lovell, Aldrin, and other Gemini astronauts demonstrated the value of orbital imagery for studying Earth’s surface. Their images helped scientists make the case for a dedicated Earth observation satellite program. One of strongest advocates for accelerating the use of Earth-observing satellites was William T. Pecora, the director of the United States Geological Survey from 1965 to 1971. In a 1969 statement, Pecora noted that the Earth Resources Observation Satellite (EROS) program he championed, and which later paved the way for Landsat , was “conceived in 1966 largely as a direct result of the demonstrated utility of Mercury and Gemini orbital photography to Earth resource studies.” For more than five decades, Landsat and other Earth-observing satellites have provided invaluable data used around the world to monitor crops, wildfires, flooding, vegetation health, land use, and countless other changes to our planet.
